The **Feedback** button can request progressive hints from a configured AI
model. **Check** still works without an AI service. API credentials and the
chosen model remain in the student's browser.

When feedback is requested, the model receives the task, the student's current
work, the checker result, the current hint level, and relevant explanatory text
from the page. The examples below show how an author controls that context.

## Automatic section context

No author option is needed for automatic context. The nearest preceding
heading starts a context section. Visible prose, lists, and callouts after that
heading are collected until the exercise; code blocks and other exercises are
excluded. A new heading starts a new section. The most recent whole blocks are
retained up to 1,500 characters, without cutting a formula. Use explicit context
for explanations that exceed this limit. This keeps feedback grounded in the local explanation
without sending the whole page.

::: {.callout-note title="Automatically collected context"}
For $ax^2+bx+c=0$, the discriminant is $D=b^2-4ac$. The sign of $D$ determines
the number of real roots. This visible callout is automatically available to
the feedback model for the exercise immediately below it.
:::

```{math-exercise}
#| label: ai-auto-context
#| vars: a,b,c
#| field-labels: Discriminant
For $2x^2+3x-2=0$, compute the discriminant: _[25]
```

## Reusable explicit context

An explicitly identified context block can be reused by exercises elsewhere on
the page. The block remains visible to students, and the exercise refers to it
by id with `context: newton-rule`. Multiple ids may be listed when a task needs
several sources. Explicit context is read from the rendered page when feedback
is requested, so mathematical notation and text generated by other Quarto
extensions are included.

::: {#newton-rule .math-exercise-context}
::: {.callout-tip title="Explicit feedback context: Newton's method"}
Newton's method uses
$x_{k+1}=x_k-f(x_k)/f'(x_k)$. Evaluate the function and derivative at the
current iterate before forming the next iterate.
:::
:::

<details class="math-example-source">
<summary>Show context-block source</summary>

```markdown
::: {#newton-rule .math-exercise-context}
Newton's method uses
$x_{k+1}=x_k-f(x_k)/f'(x_k)$. Evaluate the function and derivative at the
current iterate before forming the next iterate.
:::
```

</details>

```{math-exercise}
#| label: ai-explicit-context
#| context: newton-rule
#| mode: numeric
#| tolerance: 0.001
For $f(x)=x^2-2$ and $x_0=1.5$, compute $x_1$: _[17/12]
```

## Several exercises sharing one context

```{math-exercise}
#| label: ai-explicit-context-second
#| context: newton-rule
#| vars: x
For $f(x)=x^3-1$, write the Newton update as a function of $x_k$:
__[x-(x^3-1)/(3*x^2)]
```

## Opting out of context

Use `context: none` when surrounding prose should not be sent with a feedback
request. This disables both automatic collection and accidental inheritance
from the current section.

```{math-exercise}
#| label: ai-no-context
#| context: none
Compute $12/3$: _[4]
```

## Multi-field feedback

Meaningful labels make hints clearer and prevent generic references such as
“field 2”.

```{math-exercise}
#| label: ai-field-labels
#| vars: x
#| field-labels: Derivative, Value at x=2, Tangent slope
For $f(x)=x^3$, enter $f'(x)=$ _[3*x^2], $f'(2)=$ _[12], and the slope of the
tangent at $x=2$: _[12].
```

## Mathematics in AI context

Mathematics is sent as LaTeX source, including fractions, powers, subscripts,
matrices and aligned equations. The source is preserved before typesetting, so
MathJax and KaTeX produce the same mathematical context. The question and its
caption are preserved too; loading another pool question refreshes its source.

::: {#solenoid-notation .math-exercise-context}
A long solenoid has $N$ turns over a length $l$. Its turn density is
$n=\frac{N}{l}$, measured in $\mathrm{m}^{-1}$. In vacuum,
$\mu_0\approx 4\pi\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm{H/m}$.
For radius $2a$, the ideal long-solenoid approximation gives

$$
L=\frac{4\pi\mu_0N^2a^2}{l}.
$$
:::

```{math-exercise}
#| label: ai-solenoid-source
#| caption: Turn density
#| context: solenoid-notation
#| vars: N,l
#| field-labels: Turn density
Write the turn density in terms of $N$ and $l$: _[N/l]
```

For this example, the outgoing context retains `\frac{N}{l}` and `10^{-7}`.
To inspect it, open your browser's Network panel, request feedback, and inspect
`messages[1].content` in the chat-completions request. The `<task>` block uses
`[Turn density]` for the input; the answer stored by the checker is not copied
into that block.

## Working with different AI providers

The model capability adapter uses a portable request body for unknown
OpenAI-compatible providers. It adds low-reasoning controls only for recognised
model families and retries once with the portable baseline if a provider
rejects optional parameters. See the
[adapter design notes](docs/model-capability-adapter.md) for the policy and
known limitations.
